_doc: HMTc Category 6 (Seafood) compiler config. Method v2.0 (government-limit default). Every published cell is an EXPLICIT register-id LOOKUP against data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv (occurrence never selects a number). Built 2026-08-14 to apply the adversarial audit: (1) it REPRODUCES the live gov-limit bindings previously compiled by seafood-config.json into data/workbench/standards/cat1-compiled/{fish-*,shellfish,cephalopods,canned-seafood,seaweed-kelp-foods}.json (those 7 files are misfiled Cat-6 orphans in the Cat-1 directory and are deleted by this build), OR binds a STRICTER sovereign; (2) it fills the four mandatory panel analytes the old seafood panel omitted — total Cr (HK Cap 132V fish 1000 / India all-fishery 12000), Ni (EU 2024/1987 seaweed 30000; animal seafood has no Ni ML -> control), Al (no seafood Al contaminant ML anywhere -> control), and Cr-VI (speciation-bounded by total Cr, no food Cr-VI ML -> not-material); (3) it applies the two CONFIRMED seaweed tightenings from the French CSHPF edible-seaweed maxima (ANSES 2017-SA-0070 Table 3): Cd 2000->500 (fr_cshpf_seaweed_cd_500) and tHg 2500->100 (fr_cshpf_seaweed_thg_100), both dry-matter (mg/kg DM). MeHg on the six animal-seafood subcats is preserved as speciation-bounded by tHg (audit-affirmed: MeHg <= tHg and every binding tHg ceiling sits below the lowest applicable sovereign MeHg ML). BASIS DISCIPLINE (load-bearing): the six animal-seafood subcats are as-consumed WET weight (ppb); the seaweed subcat is DRY-weight (mg/kg DM) and its numbers must NEVER be numerically compared against the wet-weight fish ppb. The French Cd/tHg/Sn tightenings and the IL dried-seaweed rows are themselves dry-matter, so they are basis-consistent with the seaweed cell.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; explicit-id lookup; MeHg speciation-bounded by tHg on animal seafood; seaweed on dry-matter basis)

fish-marine-predatory.name: Marine predatory fish (tuna, swordfish, shark, king mackerel, marlin, billfish)

Pb.basis_label: edible portion, wet weight. Predatory-fish-specific lead: Costa Rica RTCR 409:2008 sets tuna/bonito Pb 200 (stricter than the EU general fish-muscle 300, retained as concurring context).

Cd.basis_label: edible portion, wet weight. General fish-muscle cadmium 50 (the strictest sovereign floor); the higher predatory-species carve-outs (tuna 100, swordfish 300) are looser and not adopted, so certification holds predatory fish to the general 50.

tAs.basis_label: edible portion, wet weight; total arsenic. Strictest sovereign fish total-As is 1000 (Paraguay/Singapore/Israel concur).

iAs.basis_label: edible portion, wet weight; inorganic arsenic. EU Reg. 2025/1891 muscle-meat-of-fish (other) iAs 100, HK Cap 132V fish iAs 100 concur.

tHg.basis_label: edible portion, wet weight; total mercury. Predatory species (tuna, swordfish, shark, marlin, king mackerel) bind the EU 2023/915 higher-mercury-fish ceiling of 1000; the general 500 does not apply to these listed higher-mercury species.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is the organomercury speciation of total mercury and is arithmetically bounded by it (MeHg <= tHg). The binding total-mercury ceiling for predatory fish (1000) is equal to or stricter than the lowest applicable sovereign methylmercury ML for predatory fish (MX/PH/TT/TH/US predatory MeHg 1000), so passing tHg guarantees MeHg compliance and no separate methylmercury ceiling is published. Audit-affirmed (2026-08-14).
not_material.reference_method: Total-mercury screen; reflex MeHg speciation is optional and cannot exceed the tHg ceiling.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the total-Hg predatory-fish ceiling (EU 2023/915, 1000); no sovereign MeHg ML sits below it
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU; US-FDA; MX; PH; TT; TH; GSO; HK

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a nickel maximum level for fish or fishery products anywhere in the register or (audit-verified) worldwide — EU 2024/1987 nickel covers plant foods and seaweed only, not animal seafood. Nickel is screened rather than assigned an invented or mis-based number.
control.reference_method: Total-nickel screen (ICP-MS); no sovereign fish/fishery Ni ML.
control.trigger: periodic nickel screen; flag on anomalous elevation

not_material.rationale: Fresh/frozen predatory fish has no tinplate contact; inorganic tin is a can-migration analyte. A full register Sn sweep (audit-affirmed 2026-08-14) shows every seafood tin ML is canned/tinplate-migration scope or a canned 'any food' catch-all at the ~250 mg/kg migration ceiling; no sovereign sets a non-canned fish tin matrix limit. If the product is canned it is certified under the canned-seafood subcategory tin limit.
not_material.reference_method: Packaging control (non-tinplate); ICP-MS per-lot screen; escalate to the canned-seafood Sn limit if packaged in tinplate.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No non-canned fish Sn ML; canned-seafood Sn limits are can-only
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: Codex CXS 193; EU; US-FDA; MX; CR; HK

control.rationale: No credible regulator sets an aluminium contaminant maximum level for seafood in any checked jurisdiction (the only register 'all food' aluminium row, China 100000, is an aluminium-ADDITIVE use limit, not a contaminant ML, and does not apply). Aluminium in fish is background; dietary aluminium is managed by weekly intake against the EFSA/JECFA TWI, not by a per-food maximum level. Screened rather than aligned to a non-existent ML.
control.reference_method: Total-aluminium screen (ICP-MS); managed by intake vs the EFSA/JECFA TWI; no per-food seafood contaminant ML to align to.
control.trigger: periodic aluminium screen; flag on anomalous elevation

Cr.basis_label: edible portion, wet weight; total chromium. Hong Kong Cap 132V regulates total chromium in fish at 1.0 mg/kg (1000); the only other on-scope sovereign (India FSSAI all-fishery-products 12000) is 12x looser and not adopted.

not_material.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is the Cr(VI) speciation of chromium and is bounded by the total-chromium government limit (Cr-VI <= total Cr), which binds at 1000 for fish. No jurisdiction sets a Cr-VI food maximum level, and in a reducing animal-tissue matrix Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(III), so there is no chromate pathway in fish (unlike lead-chromate-adulterated spices). Rebuttable if a routed source reports hexavalent chromium in fish.
not_material.reference_method: Bounded by the total-chromium government limit; reflex Cr-VI speciation only on anomalously elevated total chromium.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No Cr-VI food ML anywhere; bounded by total chromium (HK fish 1000)
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU; Codex; US-FDA; HK; EPA (water only)

fish-marine-predatory.scope_note: Marine predatory finfish (tuna, swordfish, shark, king mackerel, marlin, billfish), fresh or frozen, edible portion. Lead binds the predatory tuna/bonito 200 line; total mercury binds the EU higher-mercury-fish 1000 ceiling (not the general 500). MeHg is bounded by tHg. Total chromium binds HK fish 1000. Ni and Al are screened (no sovereign ML); Sn and Cr-VI are not-material. Canned predatory fish route to the canned-seafood subcategory.

Cd.basis_label: edible portion, wet weight. Crustacean cadmium 500 (EU 2023/915 and concurring sovereigns); the looser bivalve/gastropod cadmium (1000-2000) is not adopted.

tAs.basis_label: edible portion, wet weight; total arsenic 1000 (Singapore/Paraguay/AU-NZ molluscs).

iAs.basis_label: edible portion, wet weight; inorganic arsenic. EU Reg. 2025/1891 crabs and crab-like crustaceans iAs 100 is the strictest applicable species-specific line; other-crustaceans 200 and bivalve-other 500 are looser and not adopted.

tHg.basis_label: edible portion, wet weight; total mercury. EU 2023/915 crustaceans/molluscs general 500 (Costa Rica concurs).

Dry-matter basis matches the cell exactly.

tAs.basis_label: dried seaweed, dry-weight (mg/kg DM); total arsenic. Israel FCS 2016 dried-seaweed total-As 5000 (no stricter dried-seaweed total-As sovereign; France sets iAs not tAs for seaweed).

iAs.basis_label: dried seaweed, dry-weight (mg/kg DM); inorganic arsenic. FSANZ Schedule 19 seaweed iAs 1000 (HK Cap 132V seaweed iAs 1000 concurs); the French CSHPF seaweed iAs 3000 and Singapore 2000 are looser and not adopted.

tHg.basis_label: dried seaweed, dry-weight (mg/kg DM); total mercury. CONFIRMED TIGHTENING (2026-08-14): the French CSHPF edible-seaweed total-mercury maximum of 0.1 mg/kg DM (100) — ANSES 2017-SA-0070 Table 3, enforced by DGCCRF — binds, replacing the prior Israel dried-seaweed 2500 (retained as looser concurring context). The French 'Mercury' value is TOTAL mercury (matches this tHg cell). Dry-matter basis matches the cell exactly.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg). No jurisdiction sets a seaweed methylmercury ML (all sovereign MeHg limits are fish/fishery scope), and seaweed is a marine primary producer into which methylmercury does not biomagnify (it biomagnifies up the food chain, not into algae), so MeHg is a negligible fraction of total mercury and is bounded by the tHg ceiling (tightened to France 100 DM). Audit-affirmed (2026-08-14).
not_material.reference_method: Total-mercury screen; reflex MeHg speciation cannot exceed the tHg ceiling.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the total-Hg seaweed ceiling (France CSHPF, 100 DM); no seaweed MeHg ML anywhere

Ni.basis_label: seaweed nickel. EU Reg. 2024/1987 nickel in seaweed (except wakame) 30000 (Switzerland VHK 2026 'Seetang' 30000 concurs); the wakame variant (40000) is looser. This is the sole sovereign nickel limit reaching a seafood form.

Sn.basis_label: dried seaweed, dry-weight (mg/kg DM); tin. Unlike animal seafood (where tin is a can-migration-only analyte), the French CSHPF sets an edible-seaweed tin maximum of 5 mg/kg DM (5000) — ANSES 2017-SA-0070 Table 3 — because seaweed accumulates tin/organotin from seawater; it binds directly on the dry-matter basis, so this cell is a regulatory-alignment limit, not a not-material screen.

control.rationale: No credible regulator sets an aluminium contaminant ML for seaweed. Seaweed accumulates aluminium from seawater/sediment as background; dietary aluminium is managed by weekly intake against the EFSA/JECFA TWI, not by a per-food maximum level. Screened rather than aligned to a non-existent ML.
control.reference_method: Total-aluminium screen (ICP-MS); managed by intake vs the EFSA/JECFA TWI; no seaweed contaminant Al ML to align to.
control.trigger: periodic aluminium screen; flag on anomalous elevation

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a total-chromium maximum level for seaweed or edible algae (the HK Cap 132V total-Cr limits are fish/crustacean/oyster animal-seafood scope, and the China GB 2762 total-Cr limits are cereals/beans plant scope — neither is on-scope for a marine macroalga). Chromium(III) is an essential nutrient; trace chromium in seaweed is geologic uptake. Screened as the substrate for reflex Cr-VI speciation rather than aligned to a mis-scoped number.
control.reference_method: Total-chromium screen (ICP-MS); substrate for reflex Cr-VI speciation; no on-scope sovereign seaweed total-Cr ML.
control.trigger: reflex Cr-VI speciation only if total chromium is anomalously elevated

not_material.rationale: Cr-VI is bounded by the total-chromium screen (Cr-VI <= total Cr); no jurisdiction sets a Cr-VI food ML and there is no chromate pathway in seaweed (no lead-chromate adulteration as in spices), so any trace chromium is geologic chromium(III). Rebuttable if a routed source reports hexavalent chromium in seaweed.
not_material.reference_method: Bounded by the total-chromium screen; reflex Cr-VI speciation only on anomalously elevated total chromium.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No Cr-VI food ML anywhere; bounded by total chromium; no chromate-adulteration pathway in seaweed
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU; Codex; US-FDA; HK; EPA (water only)

seaweed-kelp-foods.scope_note: Edible dried seaweed/kelp food products (nori, wakame, kombu, dulse) sold as dried, on a DRY-WEIGHT basis (mg/kg DM) — these numbers must never be numerically compared against the wet-weight animal-seafood ppb. Cadmium (500) and total mercury (100) bind the French CSHPF edible-seaweed maxima (confirmed tightenings from 2000 and 2500). Lead 5000 and total arsenic 5000 bind the Israel dried-seaweed lines; inorganic arsenic 1000 binds FSANZ. Nickel binds EU 2024/1987 seaweed 30000; tin binds the French CSHPF seaweed 5000. MeHg and Cr-VI are not-material (speciation-bounded); aluminium and total chromium are screened (no on-scope sovereign ML). Seaweed used as a dietary supplement (>=80% dried seaweed) routes to the supplements category, which carries the separate 3000 cadmium supplement line.
